subject: Mathematics
name: Specialist Mathematics, Units 3 and 4
about: VCE, Complex numbers, calculus, vectors and inference
syllabus: VCE Mathematics Study Design (from 2023), Specialist Mathematics Units 3 and 4

points.title: Conjectures and if and only if
points.brief: A conjecture is a statement to prove or disprove. If and only if means each side implies the other: a necessary and sufficient condition.

points.title: Proof by induction in Unit 3
points.brief: Induction proves results about sums, divisibility and inequalities for every natural number.

points.title: Counterexamples
points.brief: One case where a statement fails is enough to show it is false for all.

points.title: Proofs about integers
points.brief: Results about divisibility, odd and even numbers and primes, proved directly or by contradiction.

points.title: Contrapositive and contradiction in Unit 3
points.brief: Proof by cases, by contrapositive and by contradiction, chosen to suit the statement.

points.title: Rational functions
points.brief: A quotient of two polynomials. Its graph has vertical asymptotes where the denominator is zero and may have an oblique asymptote.

points.title: Partial fractions in Unit 3
points.brief: A rational function of low degree written as a sum of partial fractions, which helps graphing and integration.

points.title: Graphs of quotient functions
points.brief: Graphs of rational and quotient functions, with their asymptotes, stationary points and points of inflection.

points.title: De Moivre's theorem
points.brief: (r cis θ)ⁿ = rⁿ cis(nθ), for powers of complex numbers.

points.title: Roots of complex numbers
points.brief: The n nth roots of a complex number, such as the roots of unity, are evenly spaced on a circle in the complex plane.

points.title: Factorising polynomials over C
points.brief: The fundamental theorem of algebra says a polynomial of degree n has n roots over C, so it factorises fully into linear factors.

points.title: Solving polynomial equations over C
points.brief: Completing the square, quadratic factors and the conjugate root theorem solve polynomial equations with real coefficients.

points.title: Implicit differentiation
points.brief: Differentiate both sides of a relation with respect to x, using the chain rule on terms in y.

points.title: Related rates
points.brief: The chain rule links rates of change, such as how fast a balloon's radius grows as air is pumped in.

points.title: Derivatives of inverse circular functions
points.brief: The derivative of arcsin(x) is 1/√(1 − x²), and of arctan(x) is 1/(1 + x²).

points.title: Second derivatives and points of inflection
points.brief: The second derivative shows concavity, and where it changes sign the graph has a point of inflection.

points.title: Graphs of antiderivatives
points.brief: The graph of a function shows the shape of its antiderivatives, which differ only by a vertical shift.

points.title: Integrals that give inverse circular functions
points.brief: Expressions such as 1/(a^2 + x^2) integrate to inverse circular functions.

points.title: Integration by substitution
points.brief: Changing the variable, u = g(x), turns an integral of f(g(x))g′(x) into an integral of f(u).

points.title: Partial fractions
points.brief: Splitting a rational function into simpler fractions so each can be integrated.

points.title: Integrating with trigonometric identities
points.brief: Identities such as sin²x = (1 − cos 2x)/2 turn hard integrals into ones that can be done.

points.title: Integration by parts
points.brief: The integral of u dv equals uv minus the integral of v du.

points.title: Volumes of solids of revolution
points.brief: Rotating a curve about an axis makes a solid with volume π times the integral of y².

points.title: Arc length and surface area
points.brief: Integrals give the length of a curve defined by parametric equations and the area of a surface formed by rotating a curve.

points.title: Differential equations
points.brief: Equations involving rates, formed from contexts in chemistry, biology and economics, and checked by substituting a solution.

points.title: Separation of variables
points.brief: Moving each variable to its own side of a differential equation and integrating both sides solves it.

points.title: Growth and decay models
points.brief: dy/dt = ky gives exponential growth or decay. The logistic model levels off at a limit.

points.title: The logistic equation
points.brief: A growth model where the rate slows as the population nears a limit, the carrying capacity.

points.title: Slope fields
points.brief: Short line segments showing the gradient at many points, sketching solution curves without solving.

points.title: Euler's method
points.brief: Step along a solution using the gradient, y(n+1) = y(n) + h f(x(n), y(n)), to approximate it.

points.title: Rectilinear motion
points.brief: Velocity is the derivative of displacement and acceleration the derivative of velocity, along a straight line.

points.title: Velocity-time graphs
points.brief: The gradient of a velocity-time graph is acceleration and the signed area under it is displacement.

points.title: Acceleration in different forms
points.brief: Acceleration can be written as dv/dt, v dv/dx or d/dx(½v²), chosen to suit the information given.

points.title: Vectors in 3D
points.brief: Vectors with i, j and k components describe position and direction in space.

points.title: Linear dependence
points.brief: Vectors are linearly dependent if one can be made from the others. Independent vectors in 3D point in genuinely different directions.

points.title: Scalar and vector resolutes
points.brief: The scalar product splits a vector into a part along another vector and a part perpendicular to it.

points.title: The vector product
points.brief: a × b gives a vector perpendicular to both, with size equal to the area of the parallelogram they form.

points.title: Angles between vectors
points.brief: The scalar product gives the angle between two vectors and shows when they are perpendicular.

points.title: Vector proofs in Unit 3
points.brief: Vectors prove results such as the diagonals of a rhombus being perpendicular.

points.title: Vector equation of a line
points.brief: r = a + tb gives every point on a line through a in the direction b.

points.title: Vector and Cartesian equations of a plane
points.brief: A plane is set by a point and a normal vector, giving ax + by + cz = d.

points.title: Vector calculus
points.brief: Differentiating a position vector gives velocity and acceleration vectors for motion along a path.

points.title: Paths of particles
points.brief: Position vectors as functions of time trace paths such as circles and ellipses, and show whether two particles collide.

points.title: Projectile motion with vectors
points.brief: A projectile's position vector combines constant horizontal velocity with vertical acceleration due to gravity.

points.title: Linear combinations of random variables
points.brief: E(aX + bY) = aE(X) + bE(Y). For independent variables, Var(aX + bY) = a²Var(X) + b²Var(Y).

points.title: The distribution of sample means
points.brief: For a large sample, the sample mean is roughly normal with mean μ and standard deviation σ/√n.

points.title: Confidence intervals for a mean
points.brief: An approximate 95% interval for μ is the sample mean ± 1.96 × σ/√n.

points.title: Hypothesis testing
points.brief: A null hypothesis is tested against an alternative, using how unlikely the sample result would be if the null were true.

points.title: p-values and significance
points.brief: A p-value below the significance level, such as 0.05, gives evidence to reject the null hypothesis.

points.title: One-tail and two-tail tests
points.brief: A one-tail test looks for a change in one direction; a two-tail test looks for a change either way.

points.title: Type I and type II errors
points.brief: A type I error rejects a true null hypothesis. A type II error fails to reject a false one.
